title: Delta/cursor read on (inserted_at, seq) + commit-lag lost-write fix; previews-not-bodies (supersedes US-40.5)

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: coding agent (or a running-session hook) reading a repo's channel incrementally
story.i_want_to: page/delta with a stable keyset cursor that never drops a late-committing row and returns bounded previews, not full bodies
story.so_that: a long session reliably sees every new post since it last read — without a lost-write gap and without pulling 100 full bodies into a hook

rationale: Supersedes the old US-40.5 (which the panel proved WRONG on two counts). (1) It keyset on (inserted_at, id) — but `id` is a random v4 UUID, reintroducing exactly the nondeterminism `seq` (bigserial, channel_post.ex:87-90) was added to kill; the cursor MUST tie-break on (inserted_at, seq), never id. (2) The architect's harder finding: a naive forward cursor has a PRE-COMMIT LOST-WRITE hazard — bigserial/inserted_at are assigned at INSERT (pre-commit), so a `since=now` cursor advanced past a row that had a lower seq but committed LATER silently drops that row forever. Close it with a commit-lag watermark (`since = last - epsilon`, or a commit-ordered cursor). Plus the architect's read-model finding: the split MUST be a DB `substring(body for N)` projection, because selecting the full column detoasts large TOASTed text — so return previews + ids, not full bodies.

background.reference: panel 'US-40.5 keyset on (inserted_at, id) -- WRONG tiebreak' + 'Read-split MUST be a DB projection substring(body for N)' + 'Three inconsistent orderings'; seq (channel_post.ex:87-90, 20260718000000:27-36); recent_page/3 + order_recent/2 (coordination.ex:453-529); Loopctl.KeysetCursor (keyset_cursor.ex:55,72,81).
background.includes: A keyset cursor on (inserted_at, seq) via KeysetCursor, a commit-lag watermark, and a DB substring projection returning previews + ids. Replaces docs/user_stories/epic_40_coordination_bus_v2/us_40.5.json.

acceptance_criteria.description: channel_recent's cursor keysets on `(inserted_at, seq)` — NEVER `id`. seq (bigserial, channel_post.ex:87-90) is the deterministic tie-breaker; a v4-UUID tie-break is a defect the panel called out. NAMED DELIVERABLE: Loopctl.KeysetCursor does NOT accept an integer second element off the shelf — `encode/3` guards `is_binary(id)` (keyset_cursor.ex:55-57) and its position type + serialize (keyset_cursor.ex:45, 85-88) embed a raw 16-byte UUID, so passing an integer `seq` raises FunctionClauseError. This story MUST generalize the (integrity-protected, tenant-bound, namespaced, tamper/cross-tenant → {:error, :invalid}) cursor to accept an INTEGER second element — either by widening encode/decode/serialize to handle both a UUID and an integer, or by adding a dedicated channel-post namespace variant — and cover it with the cursor's existing HMAC/tamper/cross-tenant test discipline. The generalization is scoped work owned by this story, not an assumed no-op. Encode the tuple as (inserted_at, seq), not (inserted_at, id).

COMMIT-LAG LOST-WRITE FIX: a forward/delta read does NOT trust a bare `since = last_seen_inserted_at`. Because inserted_at + seq are assigned pre-commit, a row with an earlier inserted_at/lower seq can commit AFTER a later row — a naive cursor at the later row's position would skip it permanently. Mitigate with a bounded look-back watermark (`effective_since = since - epsilon`, epsilon covering max plausible commit lag) OR a commit-ordered cursor, so a late-committing earlier row is re-scanned rather than lost. DELIVERY CONTRACT (stated precisely): the SERVER guarantees AT-LEAST-ONCE with a bounded, deliberate OVERLAP — the epsilon look-back re-delivers rows near the watermark, never dropping one. EXACTLY-once is achieved by the CONSUMER: the claude-config turn-boundary hook keeps a per-session high-watermark and dedups the small overlap by id/seq. The server does NOT itself guarantee exactly-once (that consumer dedup is out of scope for this epic — it lives in the companion). The direction is safe (over-deliver, never lose). Documented as the delta contract.

The delta/cursor read returns PREVIEWS + ids, NOT full bodies, by CONSUMING 40.D1's substring-projection preview builder (40.D1 owns/builds it — `fragment("substring(? for ?)", p.body, ^N)`, e.g. N=512 — this story reuses it, does not re-author it; C2 depends on D1 for exactly this shared read-model). Postgres never detoasts the full TOASTed body column; channel_post_json/1 (channel_post_controller.ex:261-273, body at :268) returns `body_preview` (bounded) + `id` + a truncated flag — full bodies are fetched only via the oracle-safe GET /:id (40.D1). This lands WITH the preview change, never after a body-cap increase (architect ordering constraint).

Ordering consistency (architect 'three inconsistent orderings' finding): the history keyset orders on `(inserted_at DESC, seq DESC)` (order_recent/2 non-delta, coordination.ex:527-529); the delta (`since` present) keeps ordering on `GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC` (order_recent/2 delta clause, coordination.ex:520-525) because an upserted slot advances updated_at not inserted_at. A re-touched slot is a DELTA concept (surfaced by since/GREATEST), NOT a history-cursor concept (the keyset walks inserted_at) — documented so the two reads stay coherent.

Cursor pages the full set of ALREADY-COMMITTED live rows without gaps or dups (a strict `(inserted_at, seq) < cursor` seek reaches every row visible when a page is read on exactly one page). The backward keyset walk does NOT claim to also return rows that COMMIT mid-walk with a position above an already-emitted cursor — that standard keyset property is deliberate: new/late-committing rows near `now` are owned by the epsilon-protected DELTA read (AC-40.C2.2), so history-downward + delta-at-head split the completeness contract rather than the backward walk overclaiming it. Returns the established `%{data, meta: %{..., next_cursor}}` shape (next_cursor when more rows exist, null when exhausted — change_controller.ex:122-127 / audit.ex:202-215 convention). Backward compatible: without a cursor, behavior is exactly US-39.3 (newest page, limit<=100, coordination.ex:38-42). Still filters expires_at > now and the explicit tenant/project scope.

acceptance_criteria_amendments.original_wording: Cursor pages the full live set without gaps or dups UNDER CONCURRENT INSERTS.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.amended_wording: Cursor pages the full set of ALREADY-COMMITTED live rows without gaps or dups; the backward keyset walk does NOT claim to also return rows that COMMIT mid-walk with a position above an already-emitted cursor.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.rationale: CONSCIOUS ACCEPT (not a silent scope cut). A descending (inserted_at, seq) keyset walk provably cannot include rows that commit ABOVE its frontier after the walk starts — that is the standard, correct keyset property, not a defect. New/late-committing rows near `now` are owned by the epsilon-protected DELTA read (AC-40.C2.2), so history-downward + delta-at-head TOGETHER still deliver the story goal ('a long session reliably sees every new post since it last read'). Reverting to the 'UNDER CONCURRENT INSERTS' wording would make AC-40.C2.5 re-assert a completeness guarantee the cursor-alone path deliberately and correctly does not make, and would contradict AC-40.C2.2. The narrowing splits the completeness contract across the two reads rather than overclaiming it on the backward walk; it is covered by TC-40.C2.1 (cursor completeness over committed rows) and TC-40.C2.3 (late-committing row delivered by the delta read).

test_cases.name: cursor pages the full set exactly once
steps: page limit=100 following next_cursor to exhaustion
expected_results: all 250 seen once; final next_cursor null; ordering deterministic via seq (no id nondeterminism)

test_cases.name: same-microsecond inserts order by seq not id
expected_results: ordered by seq DESC deterministically across repeated runs

test_cases.name: late-committing earlier row is not lost
preconditions: simulate: txn A inserts (earlier seq) but commits AFTER txn B (later seq) which a reader already cursored past
steps: reader delta-reads with the commit-lag watermark
expected_results: A's row IS delivered (re-scanned within epsilon), not silently dropped

test_cases.name: read returns bounded preview + id, not full body
expected_results: body_preview is <=N bytes with a truncated flag; full body only via GET /:id

test_cases.name: tampered/cross-tenant cursor is rejected
preconditions: a cursor minted for tenant A
steps: use it as tenant B / mutate a byte

test_cases.name: upserted slot surfaces in a since-delta
expected_results: the slot appears (GREATEST(inserted_at,updated_at) ordering), not dropped by limit

technical_notes: This REPLACES us_40.5.json (delete it). The old story's (inserted_at, id) keyset is the panel-rejected defect; do NOT carry it forward.

Keyset: WHERE (inserted_at, seq) < (cursor_inserted_at, cursor_seq) ORDER BY inserted_at DESC, seq DESC LIMIT n (history direction). Use KeysetCursor.encode(namespace, tenant_id, {inserted_at, seq}) — but note keyset_cursor.ex:55 GUARDS is_binary(id) and serialize embeds a 16-byte UUID (keyset_cursor.ex:85-88), so an integer seq raises FunctionClauseError today. Per AC-40.C2.1 this story GENERALIZES the helper to accept an integer second element (widen encode/decode/serialize/deserialize to handle both UUID and integer, or add a channel-post namespace variant) and extends its HMAC/tamper/cross-tenant tests — this is required scoped work, not a confirmation step.

Commit-lag watermark: the cleanest impl is the consumer keeping a per-session high-watermark and the server re-scanning `inserted_at >= since - epsilon` with client-side dedup by id/seq. Alternatively use a txid/commit-order column — heavier. Pick the epsilon-lookback (simpler, matches the turn-boundary consumer that already dedups by watermark). State epsilon (e.g. a few seconds).

Preview projection: select `fragment("substring(? for ?)", p.body, ^(@preview_bytes + 1))` and derive truncated? = byte_size(preview) > @preview_bytes. Never `select p` then slice in Elixir — that detoasts (architect finding). Keep the FULL body out of the list response entirely (defense against the 2MB-response and injection-blast-radius concerns).

Ordering: keep the existing split (order_recent/2, coordination.ex:520-529) — non-delta on inserted_at/seq, delta on GREATEST/seq. Do NOT unify them; the panel explicitly says a re-touched slot is a delta concept, not a cursor concept.
meta shape: reuse %{data, meta: %{limit, count, has_more, next_cursor}} (extend the current channel index meta, channel_post_controller.ex:228-231).

Sequencing: step 4, PAIRED with 40.D1 (read hardening) — both touch the read path; land previews here + the oracle-safe GET /:id there together. Depends on 40.D1 for the shared preview/full-body split.
